extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, NIH peer reviewers, NIH staff involved in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the NIH dual-level peer review process for evaluating research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including roles, scored review criteria, additional considerations, scoring rules, appeals, and post-review actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review must be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias; these core values drive NIH laws, regulations, and policies governing peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIH dual peer review system is mandated by statute (section 492 of the Public Health Service Act) and federal regulations governing Scientific Peer Review; policy is intended to promote a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory dual peer review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a dual peer review system: initial review by Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) and second-level review by Institute/Center Advisory Councils/Boards, as mandated by statute and federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by IC Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA-specified review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) specifies all review criteria and considerations to be used in evaluating applications; some FOAs (RFAs, certain Program Announcements) may include additional criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the FOA specifies otherwise, standard NIH review procedures and the NIH scoring system (NOT-OD-09-024) will be followed; other funding opportunity types (e.g., construction, fellowships) may use different criteria (see Review Criteria at a Glance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the designated federal official responsible for ensuring objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze application content and check for completeness; document and manage conflicts of interest; recruit qualified reviewers considering authority, dedication to fair reviews, collegiality, review experience, and balanced representation; assign applications to reviewers for critiques and criterion scores; attend and oversee administrative/regulatory aspects of meetings; prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Chair role
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit for applications under review and also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers receive access to grant applications approximately six weeks prior to the peer review meeting and must maintain confidentiality of peer review information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow Integrity and Confidentiality policies; meetings are closed to the public except for any open session described in the Federal Register; reviewers should not have applicants contact them to influence review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflict of interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest with specific applications following NIH guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts are managed per guidance documented on Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts; reviewers with COI are not eligible to score or discuss the conflicted application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written critique requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must prepare a written critique for each assigned application using Review Critique Templates as directed by the SRO, based on review criteria and judgment of merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques form part of the summary statement and are intended to provide constructive feedback on each scored review criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign numerical criterion scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer assigns a numerical score to each scored review criterion (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment for research grants/cooperative agreements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual criterion scores from assigned reviewers and discussants are reported to the applicant; these scores inform but are distinct from the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations on human subjects and related protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must make recommendations concerning protections for human subjects, inclusion of women/minorities/children, welfare of vertebrate animals, and other applicable protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific guidance for reviewers on Human Subjects Protection, Inclusion, Human Embryonic Stem Cells, Vertebrate Animals; these are evaluated as additional review criteria (no separate numeric score) and can affect fundability and NRFC designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget appropriateness assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may make recommendations concerning the appropriateness of budget requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Budget Information for Reviewers; budget and period support are also listed as review considerations that should not be considered in providing an overall impact score but are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant confidentiality and non-contact obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not contact reviewers to influence outcomes, send information directly to reviewers, or access review-related information; such actions have consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process; see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review for details on consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, considering the review criteria and additional review criteria as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary overall impact scores are given before meetings and may be used to determine which applications are discussed; final impact scores are given by eligible committee members for discussed applications and are averaged (mean * 10) to produce a 10–90 reported score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the project addresses an important problem or critical barrier to progress in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the five scored criteria used to inform the overall impact score; individual criterion scores are reported to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the qualifications, experience, and suitability of the principal investigator(s) and team to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration includes investigator expertise, productivity, and adequacy to the project's complexity and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research paradigms, uses novel concepts, approaches, or technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is judged relative to the field and the proposed project's potential to advance knowledge or methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses, including feasibility and potential problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the methods are rigorous and appropriate to accomplish the aims, address potential pitfalls, and include alternative strategies; Approach is often a dominant factor in assessing scientific merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses institutional support, resources, facilities, and the extent to which the environment will contribute to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of institutional commitment, collaborative opportunities, and whether the environment is conducive to the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the adequacy of protections for human subjects in studies involving humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an additional review criterion (no separate numeric score) considered in determining scientific and technical merit and in providing overall impact assessment as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses plans for inclusion and whether the proposed inclusion is appropriate for the scientific goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered as applicable without a separate numeric score; guidance exists for reviewers on inclusion policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the appropriateness and welfare protections for vertebrate animals used in proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered as applicable and may affect fundability if serious concerns are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses whether the proposed research involves hazardous materials or agents and whether appropriate safeguards are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as applicable; serious biohazard concerns can render an application Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Resubmission, Renewal, Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, reviewers evaluate resubmissions, renewals, and revisions according to criteria relevant to those application types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are considered in determining scientific and technical merit but are not scored separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (non-scored): Foreign organization status
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider whether the application is from a foreign organization as an applicable consideration (not scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such considerations should not be used in providing an overall impact score but must be noted and may inform programmatic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (non-scored): Select Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of whether listed select agents are involved in the research (non-scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as applicable; adherence to select agent regulations is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (non-scored): Resource sharing plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider the adequacy of plans for sharing resources (data, model organisms, etc.) though these are not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource sharing plans are considered in post-review programmatic decisions and may be required for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (non-scored): Authentication of key resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates plans for authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources (non-scored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate authentication reduces risks related to reproducibility and is considered by reviewers as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (non-scored): Budget and period support
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and period of support are considered (not scored) as part of the review considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not factor budget into the overall impact score but may comment on appropriateness and realism of budget requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 9-point scoring scale and scoring process
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; same scale used for overall impact and criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the meeting, assigned reviewers give separate scores for each of the five review criteria and a preliminary overall impact score; during meeting, eligible members give final impact scores for discussed applications; final overall impact score is mean of eligible members' final scores multiplied by 10 (reported 10–90). Applications not discussed are reported as ND (++ on face page) and typically rank in bottom half.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems in human subjects protection, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC-designated applications do not proceed to second level review (Advisory Council/Board) because they cannot be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile and ranking explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile represents the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year; percentiles are whole numbers and reported only for a subset of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement will identify the base used for percentile calculation; ad hoc study sections may use a different base; not all application types or ICs assign percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal eligibility and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may appeal initial review results if they believe the review process was flawed due to reviewer bias, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal policy (NOT-OD-11-064) does not apply to appeals of technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, NIH funding decisions, or decisions on MERIT award extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council/Board second-level review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards consider overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), summary statements, and Institute/Center priorities when advising on funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff examine applications and provide a grant-funding plan to Council; councils have access to applications and summary statements pending funding for that IC in that council round; Council advises the IC director, who makes final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program staff and funding plan role
rubrics_metrics.description: Program staff examine applications in light of review outcomes and IC priorities and provide a grant-funding plan to Advisory Council/Board to inform funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff consider overall impact scores, percentiles, and summary statements when developing funding recommendations; program officials listed on summary statements can provide guidance to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council Review for highly funded investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members conduct a Special Council Review of applications from investigators who currently receive $1 million or more in direct costs of NIH funding to determine whether additional funds should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review is to determine whether extra funds are appropriate and does not represent a cap on NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review next steps for applicants not funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose applications are not funded may resubmit with changes addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application; applicants should consult Next Steps guidance and may contact the NIH Program Official for advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements provide reviewer comments and scores to guide revisions; program officials can advise beyond online information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paylines and fundable score guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs publish paylines as part of funding strategies to guide applicants about likelihood of receiving funding; application scores are compared against the payline for the fiscal year when application is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paylines may be delayed at the start of fiscal years; if assigned IC does not announce a payline, program officials listed on the summary statement may provide guidance on fundability; awardees work with program officials and grants management officers post-award.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to volunteer as a reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and processes exist for researchers interested in volunteering to serve on NIH review panels; prospective reviewers should consult Becoming a Peer Reviewer and individual IC websites to contact SROs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs recruit reviewers based on scientific/technical qualifications and other considerations (authority, dedication, collegiality, experience, balanced representation).
